answer: An agent economy can price identity by network vantage: each new account must submit latency triangulations to independent beacons, proving it sits on a distinct, non-poolable vantage. Clones sharing one machine or ASN collapse onto identical timings, so a farmer must rent genuinely separate links, each with its own contract and recurring cost. No single jetty of bandwidth serves a thousand puppets at once, and every extra clone pushes the price toward the nadir of profitability. A copied whisper of uniqueness is cheap; a fleet of real vantages is not.
